title: I'm building a browser card game around Taiwanese, Egyptian and Norse myths — here's an actual duel
author: Important_Chapter_74
selftext:
I'm working on Shenlu, a story-driven card game where you choose a hero, follow their story and summon spirits in card duels. This clip is A-Ze facing Salma, recorded from the English browser demo.



I've been using AI for implementation and artwork. One concrete problem has been keeping the five language versions consistent. The English introduction originally showed Chinese gameplay screenshots, and the character names and chapter headings were baked into artwork. Translating the page text didn't fix those. I had to replace the images for each language and check what actually appeared in the browser.



That has shaped how I work with AI: change a specific part, preserve the existing game and saves, then check the visible result. Code running successfully doesn't tell me whether a new player understands their next move. That's what I'd like help with now.



The demo is free to play in your browser, with no account or installation required:

[https://martinihuang.github.io/shenlu-demo/?lang=en&utm\_source=reddit&utm\_campaign=shenlu-reddit-aigamedev](https://martinihuang.github.io/shenlu-demo/?lang=en&utm_source=reddit&utm_campaign=shenlu-reddit-aigamedev)



If you try it, where do you first hesitate about what to click or play? Desktop is a good starting point; on a phone, use landscape.
